1.name: Push Up
1.description: Basic exercise for chest, shoulders and triceps. Get into plank position with hands at shoulder width and lower your body until your chest almost touches the floor.

2.name: Pull Up
2.description: Fundamental exercise for back and biceps. Hang from a bar with overhand grip and pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.

3.name: Squat
3.description: Basic squat for legs. Lower your hips as if sitting down while keeping your back straight and knees aligned with your feet.

4.name: Dips
4.description: Parallel bar dips for triceps and chest. Support yourself on parallel bars and lower your body by bending your elbows to a 90-degree angle.

5.name: Plank
5.description: Isometric plank for core. Keep your body straight supported on forearms and toes, engaging your abs.

6.name: Muscle Up
6.description: Advanced exercise combining pull-up and dip. Perform an explosive pull-up and transition over the bar to complete a dip.

7.name: Pistol Squat
7.description: Single-leg squat. Lower completely on one leg while keeping the other extended forward.

8.name: Handstand Push Up
8.description: Push-ups in handstand position. Perform a push-up while inverted against a wall or in freestanding balance.

9.name: L-Sit
9.description: Isometric L position. Sit with legs extended and lift your entire body off the ground using only your hands.

10.name: Australian Pull Up
10.description: Horizontal pull-up for beginners. Hang from a low bar with feet on the ground and pull your chest to the bar.

11.name: Diamond Push Up
11.description: Push-ups with hands together forming a diamond shape. Greater emphasis on triceps than regular push-ups.

12.name: Chin Up
12.description: Pull-up with supinated grip. Similar to pull-up but with palms facing you, greater emphasis on biceps.

13.name: Burpee
13.description: Full body exercise. Combines a squat, plank, push-up and jump in one continuous movement.

14.name: Front Lever
14.description: Horizontal position hanging from the bar. Keep your body completely horizontal facing up.

15.name: Back Lever
15.description: Inverted horizontal position on the bar. Keep your body horizontal facing down.

16.name: Human Flag
16.description: Human flag. Keep your body horizontal while holding a vertical pole.

17.name: Archer Push Up
17.description: Archer push-up. One hand close to the body while the other extends laterally.

18.name: Tuck Planche
18.description: Planche with tucked knees. Balance on hands with body elevated and knees to chest.

19.name: Dragon Flag
19.description: Advanced core exercise. Lying face up, raise legs and hips keeping only shoulders in contact with the bench.

20.name: Hanging Leg Raise
20.description: Hanging leg raise. Hang from a bar and raise straight legs until forming a 90-degree angle.

21.name: Wall Push Up
21.description: Push-up against the wall. The most basic exercise in the push-up progression, ideal for absolute beginners.

22.name: Incline Push Up
22.description: Incline push-up with hands on elevated surface. Reduces load compared to standard push-up.

23.name: Knee Push Up
23.description: Push-up with knees supported. Modified version that reduces body load by approximately 50%.

24.name: Wide Push Up
24.description: Push-up with hands wider than shoulder width. Greater emphasis on chest.

25.name: One Arm Push Up
25.description: One-arm push-up. Advanced exercise requiring great strength and core stability.

26.name: Scapular Pull Up
26.description: Scapular activation hanging from the bar. First step to build pulling strength.

27.name: Negative Pull Up
27.description: Negative pull-up. Jump up and slowly lower controlling the movement.

28.name: Band Assisted Pull Up
28.description: Band-assisted pull-up. The band reduces the body weight you need to lift.

29.name: Weighted Pull Up
29.description: Weighted pull-up. Advanced progression to increase pulling strength.

30.name: Assisted Squat
30.description: Assisted squat holding onto something. Ideal for learning proper technique.

31.name: Box Squat
31.description: Squat to a box or bench. Helps control depth and technique.

32.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
32.description: Bulgarian split squat with rear foot elevated. Works each leg unilaterally.

33.name: Shrimp Squat
33.description: Shrimp squat. Advanced single-leg squat variation with rear leg held.

34.name: Bench Dips
34.description: Bench dips. Easier version of dips using a bench or chair.

35.name: Assisted Dips
35.description: Band or machine assisted dips. Reduces body load to build strength.

36.name: Ring Dips
36.description: Ring dips. Requires greater stability and strength than parallel bar dips.

37.name: Weighted Dips
37.description: Weighted dips. Progression to increase pushing strength.

38.name: Incline Plank
38.description: Incline plank with hands on elevated surface. Easier version of the plank.

39.name: Side Plank
39.description: Side plank. Works obliques and lateral core stability.

40.name: Plank with Leg Lift
40.description: Plank with leg raise. Increases core stability demand.

41.name: High Pull Up
41.description: High pull-up bringing bar to chest or lower. Prepares for muscle up.

42.name: Explosive Pull Up
42.description: Explosive pull-up with flight phase. Develops power needed for muscle up.

43.name: Tucked L-Sit
43.description: L-Sit with tucked knees. First progression toward full L-Sit.

44.name: V-Sit
44.description: V position with legs raised above horizontal. Advanced L-Sit progression.

45.name: Pike Push Up
45.description: Pike push-up. Simulates handstand push-up movement with less load.

46.name: Elevated Pike Push Up
46.description: Pike push-up with elevated feet. Greater shoulder load than normal pike.

47.name: Wall Handstand Push Up
47.description: Wall handstand push-up. Assisted version of freestanding handstand push-up.

48.name: Dead Bug
48.description: Core exercise lying face up moving arms and legs alternately.

49.name: Hollow Body Hold
49.description: Hollow position with lower back pressed to floor. Fundamental for gymnastics.

50.name: Knee Raise
50.description: Hanging knee raise. Easier version of hanging leg raise.

51.name: Toes to Bar
51.description: Bring feet to bar while hanging. Advanced leg raise progression.

52.name: Tuck Front Lever
52.description: Front lever with knees tucked to chest. First front lever progression.

53.name: Advanced Tuck Front Lever
53.description: Front lever with slightly extended knees. Intermediate progression.

54.name: Straddle Front Lever
54.description: Front lever with legs spread. Advanced progression toward full front lever.

55.name: Tuck Back Lever
55.description: Back lever with tucked knees. First back lever progression.

56.name: Straddle Back Lever
56.description: Back lever with legs spread. Progression toward full back lever.

57.name: Planche Lean
57.description: Planche lean in push-up position. Develops pushing strength.

58.name: Straddle Planche
58.description: Planche with legs spread. Advanced progression toward full planche.

59.name: Full Planche
59.description: Full planche with legs together and extended. One of the most difficult exercises.

60.name: Nordic Curl
60.description: Advanced hamstring exercise. Kneel with feet anchored and lower your body toward the ground controlling the movement with your hamstrings.

61.name: Calf Raises
61.description: Basic calf exercise. Standing, raise your heels off the ground contracting your calves and lower in a controlled manner.

62.name: Windshield Wipers
62.description: Advanced rotational core exercise. Hanging from the bar, raise your legs and rotate them side to side while maintaining control.

63.name: German Hang
63.description: Mobility position on rings or low bar. Hang with arms behind your body stretching shoulders and chest.

64.name: Handstand
64.description: Inverted balance on hands. Keep your body straight and aligned while supporting yourself upside down.

65.name: Pseudo Planche Push Up
65.description: Push-up with hands at hip level and body leaning forward. Prepares for the planche.

66.name: Archer Pull Up
66.description: Unilateral pull-up with one arm extended laterally. Transfers more load to one side of the body.

67.name: One Arm Pull Up
67.description: Complete pull-up using only one arm. One of the most advanced pulling exercises in calisthenics.

68.name: Clap Push Up
68.description: Explosive plyometric push-up. Push forcefully to lift your hands off the ground and clap before landing.

69.name: Korean Dips
69.description: Dips with hands behind the body on a low bar. Intensely works the triceps and shoulders.

70.name: One Leg Front Lever
70.description: Front lever with one leg extended and the other tucked. Advanced progression toward full front lever.

71.name: Advanced Tuck Planche
71.description: Planche with hips extended but knees still tucked. Progression between tuck planche and straddle planche.
